handleAdd accepts the initial [""] value because the length === 0 guard never catches the empty-string sentinel

updateCalendarAttendees is executed with the requester's credentials/context (possibly a mere attendee) while mutating the organizer's booking/calendar — unverified trust boundary crossing

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same flaw: the blacklist is lowercased but the input guest emails are not, so case-variant (uppercase) emails can bypass the blacklist check using includes().

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate attendee check is case-sensitive, so Guest@x.com is inserted even when guest@x.com already exists, producing duplicate attendee rows fed to createMany

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, existing-attendee filtering uses strict equality `guest === attendee.email` and the blacklist check only lowercases blacklist values, not the incoming `guests` (`uniqueGuests` filter). There is no normalization (e.g., `.toLowerCase()`) of `guests` or `attendee.email`, so `Guest@x.com` will not match an existing `guest@x.com` attendee and will be included in `createMany`, potentially creating duplicate attendee rows differing only by case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New guests are persisted with name: "", causing blank names in ICS attachments, email templates, and UI attendee lists

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, new attendees are created with `name: ""` (`guestsFullDetails`), and then that stored `attendee.name` is propagated into the `CalendarEvent` (`attendeesList` uses `name: attendee.name` with no fallback). Email templates also use attendee names directly (e.g., `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` builds `to: `${this.attendee.name} <${this.attendee.email}>``), so blank names will surface in emails/ICS and any UI that renders attendee names from the booking attendees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Organizer emails in email-manager.ts are constructed with an object argument ({ calEvent: calendarEvent }) while the class hierarchy expects positional arguments, likely causing undefined property access and throws when sending organizer email

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `sendAddGuestsEmails` instantiating `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` with an object `{ calEvent: calendarEvent, teamMember? }`, and the new organizer email class (`packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`) relies on `this.calEvent`/`this.teamMember` set by its superclass constructor. The diff does not show the superclass constructor signature, so the claim that the hierarchy “expects positional arguments” is not verifiable from the PR. The object-shape usage is also internally consistent with passing `teamMember`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error rendering in AddGuestsDialog.tsx leaks raw TRPC error codes to the user and applies t() to non-key messages, making the unable_to_add_guests fallback dead code

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog` the `onError` handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), ...)`. Because `message` is always a (non-empty) string when `err.message` exists, the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback is effectively unreachable. Additionally, interpolating `err.data?.code` into the toast exposes raw TRPC error codes (e.g. FORBIDDEN/NOT_FOUND) directly to the user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests anywhere in the diff for the new addGuests tRPC mutation covering authorization, blacklist filtering, dedupe, and email-send paths

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior (new tRPC mutation `addGuests` in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/_router.tsx`, handler logic in `addGuests.handler.ts` with authorization checks, blacklist filtering via `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`, deduping/attendee creation, calendar updates, and email sending via `sendAddGuestsEmails`). No test files or test changes appear anywhere in the provided diff to cover these new paths, so the finding about missing tests for this new nontrivial logic is diff-grounded and actionable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:45-47 uses AND (&&) instead of OR for isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner check, denying legitimate team admins

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. This will deny access to legitimate team admins who are not owners (and likewise owners who are not admins), since the permission gate is `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:55-60 duplicate email check is case-sensitive (strict equality) unlike the blacklist check, allowing duplicate guests and double invites

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are normalized to lowercase, but `uniqueGuests` compares `guest` to existing attendee emails with strict equality (`guest === attendee.email`) and checks the blacklist with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`. This makes duplicate/blacklisted checks case-sensitive, so inputs like `Test@x.com` vs `test@x.com` can bypass both the existing-attendee duplicate filter and the blacklist filter, potentially creating duplicate attendees and triggering multiple invites.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts has no check for cancelled/past/unconfirmed bookings, allowing guests to be added to dead events

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler fetches the booking by `id` and proceeds to update attendees / calendars and send emails without any gating on booking lifecycle state (e.g., no checks on a booking status/cancellation flag, nor any check that `booking.startTime`/`endTime` are in the future). This means (based on what’s in the diff) the mutation would run for any booking record the caller has permission for, including ones that might be cancelled or already in the past. The diff doesn’t show what fields exist or the intended product rule (it may be acceptable to add guests to past/cancelled bookings), so it’s a concrete edge-case/scoping concern but not verifiably a defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts does not enforce seatsPerTimeSlot capacity when adding guests, allowing overbooking

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation unconditionally appends new `attendees` via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and then updates the calendar (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`). While it includes `seatsPerTimeSlot` on the constructed `CalendarEvent`, there is no explicit capacity check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` before adding guests. Whether this truly causes “overbooking” depends on how seats/capacity are enforced elsewhere (not shown in this diff), but this new path does bypass any visible seat-limit validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: email-manager.ts:532-544 new guests receive the original AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of a notification that they were added by someone else
matched_golden_ids: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is that sendAddGuestsEmails misclassifies which email template to send because it iterates over the full attendees list but decides based on newGuests.includes(attendee.email), leading to new guests being treated like existing attendees. The candidate describes the same symptom: new guests get AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of an “added as guest” notification, which is the direct outcome of that logic error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:26-42 uses findFirst without scoping userId/team to the caller, allowing any attendee to add guests to any booking

adjudication.rationale: The handler does fetch the booking by `id` only (`prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })`), but it immediately enforces authorization based on the fetched booking: it allows only (a) the organizer (`booking.userId === user.id`), (b) an existing attendee of that same booking (`booking.attendees.find(...email === user.email)`), or (c) team admin/owner (`isTeamAdminOrOwner`) before proceeding. That means a random attendee of some other booking cannot add guests to an arbitrary booking just because the lookup isn't scoped. The finding’s claim that “any attendee [can] add guests to any booking” is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, requiring user to be both admin and owner and denying legitimate permission holders
No transactionality: booking.update persists attendees before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees; calendar failure leaves DB and calendar out of sync with no rollback or compensation

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB update happens first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterward the external side effect runs: `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. There is no Prisma transaction wrapping these steps and no rollback/compensation if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, so a calendar failure would leave attendees persisted in DB while the calendar update never happens (mutation would error out mid-way).

adjudication_records.issue_text: prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow with booking.userId || 0 throws unhandled NotFoundError (raw 500) when booking.userId is null, reachable by any authenticated attendee

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is loaded with `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null/undefined` (the `|| 0` strongly suggests this is possible), this will query `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw. There is no handling around this call, so it will surface as an unhandled error (likely a 500). This is reachable because the permission check allows any authenticated attendee (`isAttendee`) to proceed even when `booking.userId` is not present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleAdd allows submitting default [""] state, producing spurious validation error on untouched dialog
isInvalidEmail is never cleared on subsequent input changes, so the error persists after the user fixes input

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog` (`apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx`), `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when validation fails in `handleAdd`, but it is only cleared on the Cancel button click (`setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). The `MultiEmail` `setValue={setMultiEmailValue}` does not reset `isInvalidEmail` on subsequent input edits, so the error message can persist even after the user fixes the emails until they cancel/close the dialog.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent email normalization: blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive, allowing Guest@Example.com to bypass blacklist and be added twice via different casings

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, blacklist values are lowercased (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`) but the check uses `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`, so `Guest@Example.com` can bypass a blacklist entry `guest@example.com`. Also, duplicate prevention against existing attendees is case-sensitive (`guest === attendee.email`), so a differently-cased version of an existing attendee email can be added again. The server also doesn’t de-dupe `guests` internally (only filters against existing attendees), reinforcing the issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails' newGuests.includes(attendee.email) is case-sensitive, so case-mismatched existing attendees get re-confirmation email instead of guests-added email

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` is indeed case-sensitive, but the finding’s claimed outcome (“case-mismatched existing attendees get re-confirmation”) isn’t supported by what the diff shows. The `newGuests` array passed in comes directly from the input `guests` in `addGuestsHandler` (not from DB), and newly created attendees’ `email` values come from those same input strings (`uniqueGuests` is derived from `guests` without case normalization). So, based on the diff alone, there’s no demonstrated way for an existing attendee with case-mismatched email to be incorrectly classified as “new” and get the re-confirmation email. Any case-normalization at the DB layer (which could make this a real bug) is not shown in the diff, so the specific claim can’t be verified here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email sending failures are swallowed with a bare console.log with no error detail, response still says 'Guests added'

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which swallows the exception, logs no error details, and still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` even if emails fail. This is a concrete, diff-grounded reliability/observability concern, but the core add-guests operation (DB update + calendar update) still succeeds, so it’s not a clearly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members menu action is unconditionally shown with no gating on booking status (cancelled/rejected/past) or seats-capacity, allowing adding guests to dead bookings with CONFIRMED ICS invites

adjudication.rationale: The new menu item `{ id: "add_members" ... }` is appended to `menuItems` in `BookingListItem.tsx` without any conditional gating based on booking state (it’s added alongside other always-available actions). On the server, `addGuestsHandler` updates `booking.attendees` and then sends emails that generate ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` in both `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, with no checks for booking cancellation/rejection/past or seat capacity before doing so. This makes it possible (from what the diff shows) to add guests and emit confirmed invites even when such bookings should be immutable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission gate uses AND instead of OR, so team admin or owner (but not both) is denied

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`: `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. Given the variable name and typical permission logic, this will deny access to users who are only admin or only owner, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fallback teamId of 0 means personal bookings call isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner with 0, making the team-admin path dead code and collapsing authorization to organizer or any attendee

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, team authorization is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Passing `teamId ?? 0` only makes the team-admin/owner check false for *non-team* (personal) bookings, which is expected because there is no team to admin/own; it does not make the team path “dead code” in general (team bookings with a real teamId still hit it). The finding’s claim that this collapses auth due to the fallback is therefore a misread of what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Any attendee (guest) can add more guests, creating an unbounded transitive invitation chain

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the permission check explicitly allows any existing attendee to add guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and then permits the mutation if `isAttendee` is true (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`). Since the mutation persists new guest emails into `booking.attendees` via `createMany`, any newly-added guest who can authenticate as that email (e.g., they already have an account) will then satisfy `isAttendee` and can add more guests. There is also no limit/cap on `guests` length in the schema (`z.array(z.string().email())`), enabling unbounded growth.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update runs with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's, causing the attendee update to fail or target the wrong account

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` where `user`/`credentials` come from `ctx.user` (the caller) (`const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);`). The mutation explicitly allows non-organizers to call it (`isAttendee` check), so an attendee adding guests will run `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` using the attendee’s credentials rather than the booking organizer’s, which can fail or update the wrong connected calendar account.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dedup is done in-memory against a stale booking snapshot (TOCTOU), allowing concurrent requests/retries to create duplicate attendee rows; no unique constraint on (bookingId, email)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering against `booking.attendees` and a blacklist, but it does not dedupe within the incoming `guests` array itself (`const uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)`). The TRPC schema (`addGuests.schema.ts`) also does not enforce uniqueness. As a result, a request like `guests: ["a@example.com", "a@example.com"]` will produce two entries in `guestsFullDetails` and `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` will attempt to create duplicate attendee rows. Additionally, because the check is done against a previously-read booking snapshot, concurrent calls can both pass the check and insert duplicates unless the DB enforces a unique constraint or `createMany({ skipDuplicates: true })` is used—neither is shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email dedup comparison is case-sensitive, so differently-cased duplicate emails pass the filter

adjudication.rationale: The new guest uniqueness checks are case-sensitive. In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` refines uniqueness via `new Set(emails)` without normalizing case, so `Test@x.com` and `test@x.com` are treated as distinct. On the server, `addGuests.handler.ts` filters out existing attendees with `guest === attendee.email` and checks blacklist with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where the blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is not, so differently-cased duplicates can pass and be inserted via `createMany`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: System bookings with null userId cause findFirstOrThrow({id: 0}) to throw Prisma P2025, resulting in unhandled 500 instead of 4xx

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is loaded via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If a booking can have `userId` null (e.g., “system bookings”), this falls back to `0` and will trigger Prisma’s not-found error (P2025), which would surface as an unhandled 500 rather than a controlled 4xx TRPCError. This failure mode is directly present in the added code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email dispatch uses raw unfiltered guests list instead of uniqueGuests, resending confirmation emails to existing attendees and letting blacklisted emails influence routing

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, emails are dispatched with the raw `guests` input: `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` even though the handler computes a filtered `uniqueGuests` list (excluding existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and only persists `uniqueGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, routing is based on `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide between `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Passing the unfiltered `guests` means an existing attendee email included in the request will incorrectly receive a full scheduled/confirmation email again, rather than the “guests added” notification. Similarly, blacklisted emails present in the raw list can affect this routing decision for any attendee matching that address, despite being excluded from `uniqueGuests`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateCalendarAttendees failure occurs after attendees are committed to the DB, leaving persisted guests with no emails or calendar update and no compensation (non-atomic writes)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the new guests are persisted first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is called with no error handling/rollback. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation fails but the DB write remains committed, and `sendAddGuestsEmails` is never reached (it’s after the calendar update). This creates the non-atomic, inconsistent state described in the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleAdd accepts the initial [""] value because the length === 0 guard never catches the empty-string sentinel

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, multiEmailValue is initialized to [""] and handleAdd only guards on length===0, but it then validates with ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(z.string().email()). An empty string is not a valid email, so safeParse([""]) fails and the mutation is not called; it sets isInvalidEmail instead. Therefore the diff does not show that handleAdd “accepts” the [""] sentinel.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The "" sentinel for 'no emails' is duplicated across AddGuestsDialog and MultiEmail with inconsistent truthiness checks

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two different “empty” representations: `AddGuestsDialog` initializes/resets `multiEmailValue` to `[""]` (apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx), while `MultiEmail` treats “no emails yet” as an empty array (`!value.length` branch in packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx) and also pushes `""` as a new entry. This makes `AddGuestsDialog`’s `if (multiEmailValue.length === 0) return;` check ineffective with its chosen sentinel (it will be length 1), but this results in a validation error rather than a clear functional failure. It’s a real, diff-grounded consistency/maintainability issue and a minor UX edge case, not a clear correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmail uses array index as React key over an editable list with splice removal, causing wrong DOM node reuse for input state

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the list of `EmailField`s is rendered with `value.map((field, index) => <li key={index}>...)` and items can be removed via `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`. Using the array index as a key in an editable/removable list can cause React to reuse DOM nodes for different emails after a removal, leading to incorrect input DOM state/focus/cursor behavior even though the value is controlled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization logic in addGuests.handler.ts uses && instead of || for isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner, so a user must be both admin AND owner; admins or owners alone are silently denied permission

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` between `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)`, meaning the user must be both an admin and an owner to pass that branch. The subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) ...` will therefore deny access to admins-who-aren't-owners and owners-who-aren't-admins. Given the variable name and typical authorization intent, this is a correctness/authorization defect in the diff-grounded logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts passes raw guests instead of filtered uniqueGuests to sendAddGuestsEmails, so filtered-out attendees may incorrectly receive the AttendeeScheduledEmail

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the guests actually added to the booking are filtered into `uniqueGuests` and persisted via `createMany` using `guestsFullDetails` derived from `uniqueGuests`. However, the email notification call uses the unfiltered `guests` input: `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the `newGuests` list is used to decide per attendee whether to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (`if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))`). If the user submitted an email that was filtered out (e.g., already an existing attendee), that existing attendee will still match `guests` and incorrectly receive the "scheduled" email path even though they were not newly added. This is a verifiable behavioral defect from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission gate allows any attendee (isAttendee) to add unlimited further guests, escalating guest privileges beyond organizer/team-admin management

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the authorization explicitly permits any existing attendee to add guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the guard only blocks when `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee` (so `isAttendee` is sufficient to proceed). There is also no cap/limit enforced on `guests` beyond uniqueness/blacklist filtering (`uniqueGuests`), so an attendee can add an arbitrary number of additional attendees, bypassing organizer/team-admin control and potentially exceeding event constraints (e.g., no check against `seatsPerTimeSlot`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && requiring user to be both team admin AND team owner instead of ||, denying team admins permission
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the permission check uses && (requiring both admin and owner) and should use || so either role grants permission, which is the same underlying logic bug described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email comparisons are case-sensitive: blacklisted emails are lowercased but guest emails are compared verbatim, allowing blacklist and duplicate-attendee checks to be bypassed via case differences

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are normalized via `.toLowerCase()`, but filtering uses `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`. Similarly, duplicate-attendee prevention uses strict equality `guest === attendee.email` without normalization. This makes both checks case-sensitive, so a guest email with different casing can bypass blacklist and existing-attendee checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests allows any authenticated attendee to add arbitrary guest emails, persisting them as BookingAttendees, sending platform-branded ICS invites with reply-to of the organizer, and pushing attacker-chosen emails onto the organizer's live calendar event including video meeting password — spam/phishing vector with no rate limit, guest cap, or organizer confirmation

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation explicitly permits any authenticated attendee (`isAttendee = booking.attendees.find(...)`) to add guest emails (no additional authorization beyond being an attendee/organizer/admin) in `addGuests.handler.ts`. It then persists them via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, where `evt` includes `videoCallData` (meeting password/url) copied from `booking.references`. It also sends ICS/email notifications (`sendAddGuestsEmails`) with organizer-branded from/reply-to fields. There is no guest cap, organizer confirmation, or rate limiting in the diff, making the described spam/phishing vector a real security issue introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Catch block swallows the error with only console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails'), discarding err and providing no audit trail of email send failures

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`. The caught `err` is not logged or reported, and the handler proceeds to return success, so email delivery failures become hard to diagnose/audit. This is a real, diff-grounded observability/reliability concern rather than a definite correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateCalendarAttendees is executed with the requester's credentials/context (possibly a mere attendee) while mutating the organizer's booking/calendar — unverified trust boundary crossing

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, permission allows a mere attendee to call the mutation (`isAttendee` check), but the external calendar sync is performed using the *requester’s* context/credentials: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials }); await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. Since `booking.userId` may be a different organizer, this crosses a trust boundary and can cause either unauthorized modification attempts or incorrect calendar updates (using attendee creds to update an organizer-owned booking/calendar integration).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test files exist in the diff for any of the new or changed behavior (addGuests handler, AddGuestsDialog, MultiEmail, sendAddGuestsEmails, email templates)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior (viewer.bookings.addGuests TRPC route + handler, new AddGuestsDialog UI, new MultiEmail component, new sendAddGuestsEmails flow, and new email templates/subjects), but no test files (e.g., *.test.ts/tsx, __tests__ additions) are included anywhere in the changes shown. This is a concrete, diff-verifiable gap for newly introduced nontrivial logic rather than a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:35 initial state useState([""]) causes handleAdd on a fresh dialog to always fail .email() validation and show the error banner instead of being a no-op; the empty-length guard can never trigger
matched_golden_ids: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: initializing the emails/guests state as [""] (array with an empty string) leads to immediate/inevitable validation failures (e.g., .email()) and prevents empty-state logic (like an empty-length guard) from working. The golden comment suggests starting with [] and handling empty state, which aligns with the candidate’s described failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: email-manager.ts:543 compares newGuests against raw guests input instead of uniqueGuests (post-filter), so blacklisted/duplicate guests are double-counted in email selection

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server filters the requested `guests` into `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and only creates attendees from `uniqueGuests`, but it then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the *raw* input array. In `email-manager.ts` `sendAddGuestsEmails`, attendee emails are classified via `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide which template to send. Passing the unfiltered `guests` means an email that was already an attendee (and thus not newly added) can still be treated as “new” and receive the wrong email template. The diff shows this mismatch directly; it should pass `uniqueGuests` (or otherwise the actually-added emails).

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:63-64 — team admin/owner permission check uses AND instead of OR, requiring a user to be both admin and owner; denies legitimate team admins and may incorrectly allow non-team users depending on isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner handling of teamId 0

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`:
```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```
This requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner, contradicting the intent implied by the name and typical permission models (admin OR owner). As a result, legitimate team admins (who are not owners) would be denied by the subsequent permission gate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:73-77 — attendee email comparison is case-sensitive (emails only lowercased for blacklist), allowing duplicate attendee rows with different-cased emails that pollute the attendee list and calendar event

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with a case-sensitive comparison against existing attendees: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and blacklist emails are lowercased but `guest` is not (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). Since neither the schema (`z.string().email()`) nor the handler normalizes to lowercase, a guest like `Test@Example.com` can be added even if `test@example.com` is already an attendee, leading to duplicate attendee rows differing only by case and impacting the attendee list/calendar update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:118-127 — guests are written to BookingAttendee with empty name: "", causing downstream consumers like ICS generation and email headers to produce 'Nameless' <email> or misinterpret rows

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, new BookingAttendee records are created with `name: ""` (see `guestsFullDetails` used in `attendees.createMany`). The diff does show downstream usage of `attendee.name` in email payload formatting (e.g., `to: `${this.attendee.name} <${this.attendee.email}>`` in `attendee-add-guests-email.ts`) and in the constructed `CalendarEvent` attendees list, so empty names can lead to blank display names in emails/ICS. However, the specific claim about producing `'Nameless' <email>` is not supported by the diff (the `'Nameless'` fallback is applied to the organizer name, not attendee names), and it’s not verifiable from the diff alone that empty attendee names break correctness vs. being an acceptable UX/data-quality tradeoff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:159-163 — non-atomic write: attendees are committed to DB before calendar-update and email calls, with failures swallowed and no rollback or compensating delete, leaving DB state diverged from calendar state

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the DB is updated first via prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...) and committed before calling eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) and sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests). If updateCalendarAttendees throws (it’s awaited without a transaction), the mutation fails after the DB change, leaving calendars not updated. Email failures are explicitly swallowed in a try/catch with only a console.log, also with no compensating action. The diff shows no transaction/rollback/compensating delete, so state can diverge.
